name: Gadi Eisenkot
role: Leader of the Yashar list, former IDF chief of staff; reported holder of the first mandate to form a government
wants: Form a government on the first mandate, inside the 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension that the law allows (stated; Basic Law: The Government, verify section numbers).
A coalition wide enough to survive without depending on any one small party (inferred).
fears: Running out the mandate clock and handing the chance to Netanyahu or to a second election (inferred; the 2019 to 2021 pattern in br-israel-election-to-government).
A coalition that needs outside support from Arab parties and splits his own voters (inferred).
constraints: Yashar did not win the most seats and his bloc won fewer seats than Netanyahu's (fc-il-yashar-most-seats, fc-il-netanyahu-bloc-more-seats).
Since 2013, 3 of 7 Israeli elections produced a sworn-in government within 65 days, and none of the four hung results of 2019 to 2021 did (br-israel-election-to-government).
who_can_remove_them: The President, when the mandate period ends without a government (stated; Basic Law: The Government).
His own list, if it fractures during talks (inferred).
tells: Reports in the Hebrew press of signed coalition agreements, ministry allocations, or a date for the swearing-in.
Likud or Haredi parties publicly entering talks with him.

record.what: Election: Yashar not the largest party; market favorite for next prime minister

open_questions: Who are the signed partners, and does the arithmetic reach 61 without Likud?
Confirm the mandate date from the President's Residence; the clock runs from it.
